summary: Certified missing primorial gaps 20, 32, 86 and 88 as two- and three-qubit cost circuits: decide whether any device question survives the noise-model prediction, and reproduce Ziller's table of missing differences.
scope: Exact certificates, the Kingston noise prediction and the hardware decision for the primorial quotient, phase-gradient and QAOA circuits; a reproduction of Ziller Table 1 by the exhaustive search. Provider acquisitions need their own approved cases.
next_action: None. A hardware case reopens only on a platform whose compiled signal and null arms differ in physical pulses, or on a coherent family whose null-subtracted residual reaches the budget's standard deviation.

reconciliation.note: The user asked for the verified mathematics and a simulator run whose analysis decides on hardware; the certificates and the Kaggle CPU prediction are retained, and no provider job was sent.

steps.action: Decide whether a phase-gradient or null-arm run on a named platform answers a device question the Fez and Kingston atlas does not.
steps.acceptance: Either an approved written case naming platform, path, coherent family, shots and seconds or credits, or a closure stating that no such question exists.

receipts.result: No device question survives: on both Kingston paths the gap-88 and null arms drive identical pulses; static ZZ (2 to 20 kHz) leaves null-subtracted biases of at most 0.00038, fixed tilts (0.005 to 0.02 rad) at most 0.0055, and tilt at each qubit's sx gate-error bound at most 0.0159, below the 0.0188 and 0.0186 coefficient SDs at the retained budgets; IQM and Tuna-17 carry the gradient angles as frame changes or exact grid angles.

steps.action: Run primorial_cover's exhaustive search over every even difference up to the largest difference Table 1 lists for k up to 20 and compare the missing set with Ziller Table 1, p. 12.
steps.acceptance: A retained record and gate listing every missing difference per k; any disagreement with Table 1 is a finding with its exclusion or cover witness. Stop at k = 20 or when one k exceeds one hour on the build host.

receipts.result: Every Table 1 row k = 1..20 reproduces: the missing sets and N_min(k) agree, and h(k) lies in D(k); 637 cells, 9 exclusions, the slowest k well under one hour (whole run about 190 s wall on the build host).

resolution: Both obligations closed: Ziller Table 1 reproduces for k = 1..20, and no primorial-specific device question survives the null-subtracted prediction with static ZZ and axis tilt added; no provider job was sent.

receipts.result: Every step is done with its receipt: the Table 1 reproduction record and the null-residual record that closes the device question.
